title: News feed
summary: Fan-out on write vs read, celebrity handling and ranking.
prompt: Design the home feed for a social network: users follow others and see a ranked feed of recent posts from people they follow. Some accounts have tens of millions of followers.

requirements: Functional: publish a post; read a paginated, ranked home feed; follow and unfollow.
Non-functional: feed loads in ~200 ms; a new post reaches followers within seconds to a minute; highly available, eventually consistent.
estimation: 300M daily users; 30M posts a day; average 200 followers ⇒ 6B feed inserts a day ≈ 70,000/s if every post fans out.
Keep ~500 post IDs per active feed: 300M × 500 × 8 bytes ≈ 1.2 TB of feed cache before overhead.
api: GET /feed?cursor=&limit=20 → posts with authors, counts and next cursor.
data: posts(post_id, author_id, created_at, body, media) keyed by post_id; author timelines by (author_id, created_at).
follows(follower_id, followee_id) with indexes in both directions.
feed cache: user_id → list of recent (post_id, score) entries.
design: Publish: store the post, then emit an event. Fan-out workers append the post ID to each follower’s cached feed.
Celebrities (above a follower threshold) skip fan-out; their recent posts are merged in at read time.
Read: get the precomputed feed, merge celebrity posts, rank, hydrate post and author details from caches.
deepDives: Hybrid fan-out: push for typical accounts (cheap reads), pull for huge accounts (avoids millions of writes per post).
Inactive users: do not fan out to users who have not visited in weeks; rebuild their feed on next login from followees’ timelines.
Ranking: a light model scores candidates using recency, affinity and engagement; candidate generation stays simple and fast.
Deletes and unfollows: filter at read time by checking post status and the follow graph, then clean caches lazily.
bottlenecks: Fan-out backlog during spikes: queue it; freshness slips by seconds while reads stay fast.
Hot posts: cache counters and hydrate from a shared cache.
Feed cache memory: cap entries per user and expire inactive users.
tradeoffs: Fan-out on write = fast reads, expensive writes; on read = cheap writes, slow reads. The hybrid uses each where it is cheap.
Eventual consistency: a follower may see a post a few seconds late.
Ranked feeds raise engagement but are harder to debug and explain than chronological ones.

rubric.text: Compared fan-out on write and on read with numbers.
Handled celebrity accounts with a hybrid approach.
Precomputed feeds in a cache with bounded size.
Separated candidate generation, ranking and hydration.
Handled deletes, unfollows and privacy at read time.
Estimated write amplification and cache memory.
Skipped fan-out to inactive users and planned rebuilds.
Discussed ranking trade-offs and how to measure feed quality.
